revisits.note: Coin-bulge generation-side experiment (v0.13, docs/sonnet-instruction-20260720-katachi-coin-bulge-study.md): author observation verbatim -- 'CoinSRFで言うとコイン部分が平べったくなっているから一つ一つのコインがふっくらとして結果サポートが不要な形になっていると自然になりそうだなと考えている'. This is a HYPOTHESIS under test, not a settled conclusion -- UI/README/history/reports say only 'コインのふくらみ候補' / '内部サポート危険域の推定比較', never 'サポート不要'/'印刷可能'/'安全'. A/B proposal logic, gate thresholds, tutorial, and coin center/radius/placement/Patch-ID/adjacency-graph generation are all unchanged. New SkinParams.coinBulge (default 0, UI range 0-0.32, step 0.005, label 'コインのふくらみ') widens ONLY the coin-shape shell band in plate mode from thickness/2 to thickness/2+coinBulge, letting a coin's own round point geometry push outward on both sides of the host surface up to its raw (unclipped) extent; flatRing/ring3d/window mode are entirely unaffected. coinBulge<=0 runs the EXACT pre-existing code path (coin+flatRing unioned into one field, then intersected with the shell once) rather than 'split with a zero-width extra band', because smooth booleans (opSmoothIntersection) are not distributive -- intersection(shell, union(coin,flatRing)) is not guaranteed to numerically equal union(intersection(shell,coin), intersection(shell,flatRing)) even at zero extra width, so a literal separate branch was required to guarantee old-recipe replay produces byte-identical results. Implemented identically in CPU (field.ts's compositeSdf, new hostBandSdf helper shared with shellSdf) and GLSL (shaders.ts): extended the uPatchData[i].y fractional shape encoding from a single ring3d bit to three shapes (coin +0.00, flatRing +0.25, ring3d +0.50), decoded via isCoinPoint/isFlatRingPoint/isRingPoint, no new uniform arrays (only one new scalar uCoinBulge). Enumerated every compositeSdf call site via `rg -n "compositeSdf\("` and threaded coinBulge through all of them explicitly (never an implicit default): picking.ts (raymarchComposite/estimateCompositeNormal), meshExport.ts (buildSkinMesh), partition.ts (buildPartitionMeshes, 6 internal call sites), renderer.ts's update() uniform write, and every main.ts call site. coinBulge is a live field-shape parameter read by compositeSdf for every EXISTING patch (unlike minR/maxR/irregularity/gap/attempts/patchShape/ring-specific knobs, which only affect patches created by a future 詰める) -- extended this round's invalidation to thickness/roundK too (instruction §3.2 explicitly permits this 'if the common-function route is safer/minimal'): changing any of the three now invalidates a built partition result/Worker/export/metrics via the existing invalidateStalePartitionResult() (new thin wrapper invalidateStaleResultForShapeParamChange overrides the status text to '形状設定が変わったため、同じA/B構成でも物理分割をもう一度実行してください' instead of the draft-edit wording) WITHOUT touching state.partition or the confirmed A/B grouping itself, so no re-confirm is ever required, only a rebuild -- verified: build to completion, change coinBulge, hasResult flips false, state.partition's groupA/B unchanged, draftMatchesConfirmed() stays true, real step stays at 7 (no regression to 6), and a fresh rebuild succeeds immediately. PartitionBuildRequest gained an explicit coinBulge field (never implicitly defaulted inside the Worker); partition provenance gained shapeParameters:{thickness,roundK,coinBulge}; makeSkinExportBaseName embeds coinBulge into the filename when >0 (e.g. yohaku-skin-plate-coin-bulge-0p080-20260720), unchanged at 0. Recipe formatVersion stays 1 (DEFAULT_SKIN_PARAMS.coinBulge=0, handled generically by the existing setSkinParam operation, no old-recipe compatibility work needed). UI: コインのふくらみ slider integrated into the existing skin-slider mechanism, plus static (non-recommending) preset buttons 0/+0.04/+0.08/+0.12 and a short one-line state ('0: 従来' / '>0: ふくらみ比較中'); beads-mode caption gets an explicit warning when coinBulge>0 that beads draw raw PatchPoint spheres and cannot show the shell-clipping difference, so beads must never be mistaken for a bulge preview; changing the value auto-discards any stale 全体メッシュ overlay (pre-existing afterMutation() path, unmodified) and never auto-regenerates the heavy overlay on slider drag (only an explicit 全体メッシュ selection triggers a rebuild). Verified end to end with real coordinate clicks (window.__skin used solely to read state -- getPatches/getSkinParams/getViewMode/getPartitionResult/getPartition -- never to drive an action): lightweight fixture (28-coin pack, minR/maxR widened for a coarser packing) showed identical Patch-ID/shape/point fingerprints across coinBulge=0/+0.08/+0.12 (only lateral positions matter for this check, confirmed unchanged) while the raymarch view visibly went from flat/edge-on discs to progressively rounder bumps at the same camera pose; flatRing-only and ring3d-only fixtures were pixel-identical between coinBulge=0 and +0.12; window mode was pixel-identical between 0 and +0.12 for a coin fixture. Real CoinSRF (141 coins, ID 392-532, all shape=coin, no coinBulge operation in the recipe itself so it loads at 0) compared via 全体メッシュ resolution-48 previews (beads intentionally NOT used for this comparison, per instruction §4's explicit prohibition on treating beads as a bulge preview): coinBulge=0 rendered as the flat, crinkled, overlapping-plate look matching the author's '平べったい' observation (2.75s synchronous build); +0.08 showed individually rounded, clearly puffy coin bumps with visible-but-not-collapsed valleys between neighbors (2.85s); +0.12 was more pronounced still, individual coins still distinguishable, overall CoinSRF silhouette preserved (2.84s). Honestly recorded that buildSkinMesh's 全体メッシュ path is NOT Worker-ized (unlike partition builds) and blocks the main thread synchronously for the full ~2.8s on every rebuild -- an existing limitation, not something this round introduced or fixed. No author was present in this session to select a candidate value, so per instruction §7 item 7 ('作者が候補をまだ選んでいない場合は、STLを4種類量産せず、ブラウザ比較画面で止める') this round stopped at the browser comparison screen -- §8's Optimizer diagnosis comparison (value 0 vs a chosen candidate) was NOT performed. Explicitly unconfirmed and documented as such: real slicer support-generation behavior (never tested), whether the visible valleys between bulged coins become new external support-risk regions (untested), and full-resolution (96) STL topology/watertightness at any coinBulge value (only the coarse resolution-48 preview was built). Added new src/studies/skin/coinBulge.test.ts (11 assertions: coinBulge=0 matches both the coin-only and the coin+flatRing COMBINED pre-split formula exactly, not a split-then-union; a probe point between the old shell edge and the new coin band goes solid only when bulged; bulge never extends solid material past the coin's own raw field even at bulge=5.0; flatRing-only/ring3d-only/window-mode fields are byte-identical across bulge values; computeSkinSamplingBounds already covers the coin's raw radius so a bulged mesh can never be clipped; old-recipe replay leaves coinBulge at the default 0; export/import round-trips a non-zero value exactly; buildPartitionMeshes produces different part volumes for different coinBulge, proving the value actually reaches the Worker's own builder and isn't silently dropped) plus wired it into package.json's test:partition and tsconfig.test.json's include (Worker-lifecycle interaction with a coinBulge change mid-build -- cancellation and no-late-result-adoption -- is a browser-only concern per the pre-existing documented Vite-Worker-under-Node limitation, not re-tested here beyond what v0.11's existing mechanism already covers structurally). Partition tests 102 (41+50+11), test-source typecheck, eight-page npm run build, git diff --check all passed. Partition math, A/B proposal, gate thresholds, tutorial, and Patch generation logic are all unchanged this round. Not committed; not deployed (author review pending).

Selection-visibility final polish (same-day amendment to v0.12, docs/next-agent-instruction-20260720-katachi-selection-final-polish.md; version left at 0.12.0, not bumped): the 1.2x pale-yellow wireframe outline, non-selected dimming, A/B fill-color preservation, A/B endpoint badges, the always-visible selected-patch label + assign-button disabling, and the tutorial short-line/collapsed-details were all kept as-is per instruction -- fixed only two leftover UI-state inconsistencies from the audit. P0: onToggleSeedPickMode(false) ('両端選択を中止') previously only called updateOperationFocus(), which cleared the viewport frame/chip but left seedAId and its A badge behind if only the A endpoint had been picked -- the author couldn't visually tell 'cancelled' from 'A confirmed'. Added a shared discardEndpointSelection() (clears seedAId/seedBId/seedPatchIds/draft A+B, invalidates any stale result/Worker via the existing safe path, then refreshPartitionDraft() to redraw badges/colors/tutorial/focus from the same cleared state) and now call it from BOTH onToggleSeedPickMode(false)-while-incomplete and onClearSeeds (previously duplicated inline), consolidating responsibility. Completed A+B pairs never reach the false branch -- handleClick's seed-pick branch flips seedPickMode itself the instant both are set -- so this never touches the existing 'badges persist through propose' behavior. Verified with real clicks: picked A (badge appears, switches to B-wait), pressed 'cancel', and confirmed via the read-only debug handle that getSeedIds() returned [] (seedAId/seedBId actually null, not just hidden), viewport.className emptied, the A badge disappeared, and the panel read 'A端 未選択 / B端 未選択' again. P1: computeViewportFocus() previously showed the A/B chip/frame/row-emphasis for ANY patch selection whenever patches existed and add-patch-mode was off -- even during ordinary Pack/delete/mesh-inspect work with no A/B draft, confirmed partition, or open guide, making A/B assignment look like the primary action when the author wasn't doing A/B work at all. Added a new pure derivePartitionViewportFocus(input) to partitionTutorial.ts taking an explicit inPartitionContext boolean (so the function itself never touches the UI layer, avoiding circular refresh calls) computed in main.ts from seedPickMode || (draftGroupA.size+draftGroupB.size>0) || state.partition!==null || (tutorial open && real step === 5). Also had to split the row's .action-emphasis CSS class out of setPartitionSelectedPatch (which still drives the label text and assign-button disabled state off selection alone -- assigning to A/B is still how a fresh draft gets started, so buttons stay usable outside 'context') into a new setPartitionActionEmphasis(active) called with active = focus==='selected' -- found and fixed a real bug during verification where, without this split, the emphasis border kept lighting up on ANY plain selection regardless of context, contradicting the very requirement being implemented. Verified with real clicks: right after Pack (no A/B context) the chip stayed hidden even after selecting a patch (outline/label/button-enable still worked, confirming those three are correctly NOT gated); starting endpoint selection still showed the blue/orange frames+chips+badges exactly as before; after proposing (draft now exists, real A/B context), the chip/frame/emphasis correctly reappeared and cycled between unselected and selected states; Aのみ/Bのみ filter and OrbitControls rotation showed no regression from v0.12. Added 7 new partitionTutorial.test.ts assertions for derivePartitionViewportFocus covering the instruction's 6 documented cases plus a no-patches edge case. Partition tests 91 (41+50), test-source typecheck, eight-page npm run build, git diff --check all passed. Not committed; not deployed (author review pending).

Selection visibility during A/B assignment (v0.12, docs/next-agent-instruction-20260720-katachi-selection-visibility.md): author observation verbatim -- '選択してA/Bに変更するときに選択しているものの表示を変えないと選択できているのかわからない' / '文字はあまり読まないので文字で説明は重要ではなく、今すべき操作を強調表示が大事' / '選択はかなり強調しないと今のままではわからない。A端B端を選ぶときも同じ'. Partition math, proposal, Worker, gate, and history unchanged. Root cause: renderer.ts's recolorBeads() unconditionally preferred A/B/unassigned group color over any selection color whenever a T13 grouping was active (i.e. for the entire A/B workflow) -- selecting a patch never changed its bead color at all, exactly matching the author's report. The old SELECTED_COLOR was also too close to GROUP_B_COLOR (orange-ish) to double as a recolor even if it had been wired up. Fix keeps A/B/unassigned color on the selected bead UNCONDITIONALLY (never replaced) and instead layers two independent, non-color cues: a separate small InstancedMesh ('highlightMesh') drawing an oversized (1.2x) bright pale-yellow wireframe shell over just the selected patch's own bead instances, rebuilt cheaply from existing instance matrices on every selection change (no full patchBeadMesh rebuild); and dimming every OTHER bead to 50% brightness while a selection is active (both within the instruction's 45-60%/1.15-1.25x ranges, no blink/pulse). Hidden automatically when the selected patch's own group is filtered out via Aのみ/Bのみ. Added a permanent one-line 選択中Patch: #ID / 現在 A（青） display (aria-live=polite, color swatch + text) directly above the Aへ/Bへ buttons via new pure functions resolvePartitionSelectionGroup (draft-set membership, with an explicit non-silent 'conflict' state if a patch were ever in both sets -- defensive, unreachable via the existing assign paths which always delete-then-add) and describePartitionSelectionLabel in partitionTutorial.ts; the assign buttons are now disabled while nothing is selected. Added a viewport-level 'what to do next' system (main.ts's computeViewportFocus/updateOperationFocus): a static frame (box-shadow, no layout shift) plus a floating chip cycle through 待ち (① coinをクリック, faint white frame) -> selected (② AかBを押す, frame cleared, a static non-animated .action-emphasis border+tint on the whole Aへ/Bへ row instead, both buttons shown at equal visual weight since software doesn't pick A or B) -- suppressed while in manual-add-patch mode. Extended the same visual grammar to A/B endpoint picking: starting 'A端・B端を選び直す' shows a thick blue frame + 'A端をクリック' chip; picking A switches instantly to an orange frame + 'B端をクリック' chip and adds a camera-facing canvas-texture Sprite badge (ring + big 'A' letter) pinned to the endpoint patch's own point; picking B adds the matching orange 'B' badge and ends seed-pick mode (frame/chip clear automatically since focus falls through to the manual-selection state); both badges persist through 'propose' since they're driven by seedAId/seedBId, not by pick-mode itself; '両端選択を中止' clears the frame/chip immediately (verified: viewport.className empties on the very next tick). Real bug found and fixed during implementation: the badge Sprites were built with depthTest:true and positioned at the seed patch's OWN anchor point -- i.e. dead center of an opaque bead sphere -- so they were completely invisible behind the sphere's own front face (confirmed via screenshot: zero badges visible despite correct seedAId/seedBId state). Fixed by setting depthTest:false/depthWrite:false/renderOrder:10 on the badge material so it always draws on top; verified after the fix that both A and B badges render clearly as large ringed letters floating over their coins. Tutorial text shortened per author's stated preference for minimal reading: added a `short` one-line imperative field to TutorialStepContent (e.g. Step 2: 'A端をクリック → 次に反対側のB端をクリック') shown as the card's primary always-visible content; the old multi-bullet body moved into a <details><summary>詳しく見る</summary> collapsed by default and re-collapsed on every step change. Step 5's advance ('確認した') button gained data-tutorial-target='confirm-review' added to that step's highlightTargets, so after an A/B fix the existing tutorial-highlight mechanism (unchanged otherwise) emphasizes the next real action -- only while the guide is open and the real workflow is actually at step 5, never forcing auto-confirm and never highlighting outside the guide. Verified end to end against real CoinSRF (141 coins) using only real coordinate clicks (window.__skin used solely to read state -- getSelectedPatchId/getSeedIds/getDraftGroups/getViewMode -- never to drive an action): selecting an unassigned patch showed the bright outline + '#448 / 現在 未割当', assigning to A recolored it blue while keeping the outline and updating the label to '#448 / 現在 A（青）' with the row's yellow emphasis border appearing; selecting a different (B) patch showed its own outline while #448 stayed blue at full brightness (both A/B colors visible simultaneously, only the currently-selected one highlighted); a B→A reassignment (patch #507, real click through propose -> select -> confirm label read '#507 / 現在 B（オレンジ）' -> real click 'Aへ' -> label became '#507 / 現在 A（青）', outline never dropped); re-clicking the selected patch cleared selectedPatchId, the outline, and reset the label to 'なし', re-disabling both assign buttons; switching to 'Aのみ' while a B patch was selected hid that patch AND its outline together (no orphaned outline left floating, confirmed by screenshot); orbiting the camera (real click-drag) kept both the manual-selection outline and the A/B endpoint badges correctly pinned to their target patches' new screen positions (structurally guaranteed since both are real Object3Ds in the scene graph, not screen-space overlays, but verified visually anyway). Added 10 new partitionTutorial.test.ts assertions: 4 for resolvePartitionSelectionGroup (A/B/unassigned/conflict), 5 for describePartitionSelectionLabel (all four states plus the conflict wording), 1 verifying every one of the 8 tutorial steps has a non-empty short line distinct from its title. Partition tests 84 (41+43), test-source typecheck, eight-page npm run build (skin bundle grew from ~77KB to ~83KB), git diff --check all passed. Not committed; not deployed (author review pending).

Invalidation status-text honesty correction (same-day amendment to v0.11, docs/next-agent-instruction-20260720-katachi-invalidation-status-honesty.md; version left at 0.11.0, not bumped): partition math, Worker termination, and gate thresholds unchanged -- fixed two status-display inaccuracies left by the in-flight race fix above. Problem 1: invalidateStalePartitionResult() cleared a COMPLETED result's export/metrics (hadResult=true, hadRunningWorker=false path, e.g. editing the draft after a build finished) without ever calling setPartitionStatus(), so the old '完了 ...' text stayed on screen even though partitionResult/exports/metrics were already gone underneath it. Problem 2: the always-invalidate-unconditionally policy (kept as-is, safety over precision) had a status message that always said 're-confirm', even when the edit was a no-op relative to the last confirmed configuration (e.g. clicking 'assign to A' on a patch already in A) -- re-confirming in that case is genuinely unnecessary, only a rebuild is. Fixed by adding a pure describePartitionInvalidationStatus(hadRunningWorker, stillConfirmedAfterEdit) to partitionTutorial.ts and calling it unconditionally (not just when hadRunningWorker) from invalidateStalePartitionResult(), which now also evaluates draftMatchesConfirmedPartition(draft, state.partition) right after the edit to get stillConfirmedAfterEdit; hadResult/hadRunningWorker detection, Worker termination, and result/export/metrics clearing are otherwise unchanged. Subject wording distinguishes 'an in-flight build was killed' (実行中だった分割) from 'a completed result was discarded' (前回の分割結果); stillConfirmedAfterEdit distinguishes 'もう一度確定してください' (re-confirm needed) from '確定構成は変わっていないため、もう一度物理分割してください' (rebuild only). Verified against a lightweight fixture (default 12-ball host, 51 coin patches, endpoints #4/#22, 50/1 proposal) with real coordinate clicks only (window.__skin used solely to read state -- workerRunning/hasResult/draftMatchesConfirmed/selected patch id -- never to drive an action): (a) built to completion at resolution 32 (1.3s, gate-failing but genuinely COMPLETED), then a real click moved a different patch (#25) to the opposite group (breaking the confirmed match) -- the stale '完了 (経過1.3秒) ...' text was replaced (not left showing alongside the new null result), gate-metrics text disappeared, export buttons went disabled, and the real step fell back to 6; (b) re-confirmed, started a fresh build at resolution 224 (raised via the real 解像度 slider specifically to keep the Worker alive long enough to interact with), and while workerRunning:true, a real click selected patch #4 (already in group A) and clicked 'assign to A' (a no-op relative to the confirmed groups) -- workerRunning flipped to false immediately (Worker still safely stopped), draftMatchesConfirmed() stayed true, the real step stayed at 7, and the status text read '...確定構成は変わっていないため、もう一度物理分割してください' rather than asking to re-confirm; a 3-second re-check confirmed hasResult/workerRunning both stayed false (no late Worker message adopted, unchanged from v0.11). Added 4 new partitionTutorial.test.ts assertions for describePartitionInvalidationStatus's four (hadRunningWorker, stillConfirmedAfterEdit) combinations. Partition tests 74 (41+33), test-source typecheck, eight-page npm run build, git diff --check all passed. Not committed; not deployed (author review pending).

In-flight Worker/draft race fix (v0.11, docs/next-agent-instruction-20260720-katachi-inflight-draft-fix.md): partition math, gate thresholds, and coin shapes unchanged -- this round fixed state concurrency and guide display only, not partition quality. P0: invalidateStalePartitionResult() previously started with `if (!partitionResult) return;`, which is trivially true for the ENTIRE duration of an in-flight build (partitionResult is only set on successful completion), so real draft changes made while a build was running silently no-op'd -- partitionGeneration never advanced, the running Worker kept computing against the old confirmed groups, and its late result could be adopted since the generation check also never fired. Fixed by checking `partitionResult !== null || activePartitionWorker !== null` (preserves the original no-op for the common 'nothing built yet' case) and, when either is true, unconditionally advancing partitionGeneration, terminating and nulling any active Worker, clearing setPartitionBuildRunning/partitionResult/export flags/metrics, updating the status text, and refreshing the tutorial. Chose to always invalidate rather than diff draft membership before/after (documented trade-off: a false-positive re-invalidation on an already-in-group re-click costs one redundant rebuild, avoiding diff complexity -- the status wording's separate claim that this also cost a redundant RE-CONFIRM was inaccurate and corrected same-day, see the 2026-07-20 invalidation-status-honesty entry below). Consolidated onClearSeeds's duplicated inline partitionGeneration++ + invalidation logic to call the shared function instead of running both independently. onToggleSeedPickMode/onProposeGroups/onAssignSelectedPatchToGroup/window.__skin.proposeGroups/window.__skin.assignPatchToGroup already called the shared function from a prior round, no changes needed there. Verified against real CoinSRF (141 coins, samples/CoinSRF_yohaku-skin-plate-20260717.recipe.json) using only real coordinate clicks (window.__skin used solely to observe workerRunning/partitionResult, never to drive actions): confirmed A#495/B#425 (72/69), started a real resolution-96 physical build (workerRunning:true), then mid-build moved a patch via a real click on '選択中のパッチをAへ' -- workerRunning immediately flipped to false, partitionResult stayed null, the exact alert-equivalent status text appeared, the real step fell back to 6 (visualReviewed/manualReviewed stayed true), and a 3-second re-check confirmed no late Worker result was ever adopted (hasResult/workerRunning both still false, terminated Worker's message never arrives). Re-confirming afterward restored confirmed:true and a fresh build-Worker start (workerRunning:true again on the new 72/69 draft), immediately cancelled without waiting for completion -- CoinSRF's heavy physical build was not run to completion this round, only started and discarded twice for verification. P1: added pure normalizeDisplayedStep(actualStep, displayedStep), resetting the browsed displayedStep to null (follow) whenever the real workflow regresses below it (e.g. reselecting endpoints while reading a past step via 前へ) -- called from refreshPartitionTutorial() to reset the persistent tutorialDisplayedStep module variable itself, not just clamp deriveTutorialNavState's one-shot return value (clamping only the output would leave the stale module variable to re-trigger the same wrong 'viewing past' reading on every subsequent render). Added 5 new partitionTutorial.test.ts assertions covering the instruction's three regression cases (actualStep=2/displayedStep=6 -> null; actualStep=7/displayedStep=6 -> unchanged; actualStep=6/displayedStep=6 -> follow) plus null-input and equal-step edges. Partition tests 70 (41+29), test-source typecheck, eight-page npm run build (Worker chunk included), git diff --check all passed. Not committed; not deployed (author review pending).

Post-limit audit fixes Phase B (v0.10, docs/next-agent-instruction-20260719-post-limit-audit-fixes.md): the guide did not change partition math, gate thresholds, or coin shapes. B1: added pure draftMatchesConfirmedPartition(draftA, draftB, confirmed) (set comparison, array order irrelevant, A/B swap counts as a mismatch); tutorial snapshot.confirmed now reflects this instead of state.partition!==null, and buildPartition() itself re-checks it before starting the Worker (alert 'A/Bを変更したため、もう一度「確定」してください', no Worker start on mismatch). propose/manual-assign/reseed now invalidate any stale partitionResult + export links via invalidateStalePartitionResult(). B2: added deriveTutorialNavState(actualStep, displayedStep, flags) and a session-only tutorialDisplayedStep, decoupling 'which step is being read' from derivePartitionTutorialStep's real workflow position -- 前へ/最初から読む only move the displayed page (never geometry/history/draft/review flags); 次へ while browsing a past step only turns the page and never sets visualReviewed/manualReviewed, which can only change at the real step 4/5; added a 現在の工程へ戻る(Step N) control and a 表示中/現在の工程 note while browsing; highlights are suppressed while browsing since they point at the real step's controls. Verified against real CoinSRF (141 coins) with real UI clicks (canvas endpoint picks, propose, confirm): editing the draft after confirming (moving one patch via a real click) flipped draftMatchesConfirmed() to false and the real step to 6 while visualReviewed/manualReviewed stayed true; the build button was blocked with the exact alert text and workerRunning stayed false; re-confirming restored step 7 and a real build-Worker start (immediately cancelled, the heavy compute itself was not repeated); 前へ from step 7 visibly showed Step 6/8 with the viewing-past note and 現在の工程へ戻る(Step 7), confirmed by screenshot; 最初から読む from step 7 set displayedStep=1 while actualStep/confirmed/review flags/draft counts were provably untouched. B3: tsx added as a direct devDependency (was only reached via npx, which hit the registry and failed offline with ENOTFOUND) and test:partition no longer uses npx; ran npm run test:partition with no network and confirmed all tests still pass from the local binary. Added 13 new partitionTutorial.test.ts assertions (65 total across both partition test files), test-source typecheck, eight-page npm run build, git diff --check all passed. localStorage still only persists open/visualReviewed/manualReviewed (displayedStep is an in-session module variable), old stored values remain compatible. Not committed; not deployed (author review pending).

T10 initial implementation: new Study S-skin. Host = S1 ball list + k (unchanged, imported from cloud-sculpt/field.ts, same as pack). Shell = |hostSdf| - thickness/2 (field.ts's shellSdf). Patch = an anchor point projected onto the host surface via SDF-gradient Newton descent (field.ts's projectToSurface) plus 3-8 sub-points scattered in the anchor's local tangent plane and re-projected, all smooth-min'd together with one roundK -- structurally just another Ball[]-like point list, no new distance math invented (only the placement -- points hugging a curved surface instead of floating in open space -- is new). Multiple patches are one flat union (patchesSdf), mirroring pack's void-field reuse of a single roundness knob for both intra-group blending and the boolean op with the host (仮決め, same precedent). Composite is mode-dependent: plate mode = opSmoothIntersection(shellSdf, patchesSdf, roundK) (殻∩パッチ群), window mode = opSmoothSubtraction(patchesSdf, shellSdf, roundK) (殻−パッチ群) -- both Quilez smooth booleans, written locally in field.ts (not imported from pack, keeping the Study self-contained same as pack did relative to foam). New op packPatches carries the resulting patch list (anchor+sub-points+radii) explicitly, mirroring pack's packVoids/mpm's freeze precedent -- replay never re-runs the greedy walk or the surface projection. New op setMode records the plate/window toggle itself, so mode survives export->import even though it doesn't touch the packing data (completion condition 5 explicitly wants full history reproduction). Manual patch add (click while in add-patch mode, host-only raymarch target, same simplification pack made) places a light 3-point spray rather than running the full irregularity/gap logic -- documented as not honoring gap, same as pack's manual void add. Gauges: estimateMortar (cross-patch point-pair clearance, same dual reading as pack's thinnest-wall proxy -- 'thinnest mortar' in window mode, 'closest two plates came to touching' in plate mode), estimateCoverage (two stacked Monte Carlo approximations: shell-band volume as a proxy for surface area, then patch-membership fraction within that), estimatePatchComponents (a FAST proxy -- union-find over patch-to-patch point proximity, meaningful only for plate-mode 'how many patches fused into how many pieces', explicitly documented as NOT modeling window-mode shell connectivity). The AUTHORITATIVE connected-component count T10 完了条件3 asks for is computed separately, in meshExport.ts's countConnectedComponents, via union-find over the actual generated triangle soup's shared vertices (same vertex-quantization convention as cloud-sculpt's inspectWatertight) -- this is the number the README's completion-condition verification cites, not the live proxy. Mesh export pads the host's own sampling bounds by thickness/2 on every side (the shell band extends that far past the host's raw ball-radius envelope) before delegating to buildMeshFromField. Second, and more substantive: real-coordinate click verification (AGENTS §3) found that click-to-select silently failed on every plate-mode patch -- picking.ts's 'which patch owns this point' test used a zero-surface-distance threshold (correct for window mode, where only a carved opening's rim belongs to a patch) but plate mode's visible surface is shell∩patches, so almost every rendered plate-face point sits deep inside a patch's point spheres, never near their own zero surface. Fixed by making picking.ts's nearestPatchId (and the equivalent shader onPatch/coloring logic) mode-aware: plate mode picks the nearest patch unconditionally (no threshold), window mode keeps the rim-only threshold test.
